author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Former U.S. Representative Jim Langevin is urging stronger oversight of artificial intelligence as Rhode Island expands education and policy work around the technology. Langevin, now the distinguished chair of the Institute for Cybersecurity and Emerging Technologies at Rhode Island College, said safeguards and transparency should keep pace with rapid adoption.

Langevin led Rhode Island’s AI task force, which released recommendations earlier this year. He is also considering joining a government advisory board at OpenAI, according to NBC 10 News. His comments place the state’s debate within a broader national discussion over how governments should address risks without closing off useful applications in education, public services and business.

Rhode Island College’s cybersecurity and emerging-technologies program now serves more than 500 students, giving the policy discussion a local workforce dimension. Langevin’s position combines experience in Congress with the institute’s focus on training and research. No specific new Rhode Island regulation was announced, but his call adds momentum to efforts to translate task-force recommendations into practical rules. The central question is how to require accountability from developers and users while preserving room for responsible innovation.
dek: The former congressman says transparency and safeguards should advance alongside AI adoption and workforce training.
headline: Jim Langevin calls for stronger AI oversight in Rhode Island
